the command module's main environmental: The command module’s main environmental equipment occupied the left equipment bay. Trace gas from the crew through the compressor, absorber and suit heat exchanger. The protective enclosure is open and the plumbing is spread out to show the route.
the modules sit inside a common equipmen: The modules sit inside a common equipment area. Their stained-metal rails and the open front show their mounting relationship. This display separates the equipment for visibility.
three crew members had suit connections: Three crew members had suit connections. A cabin return let atmosphere from the cabin enter the conditioning circuit.
the astronaut consumes oxygen a separate: The astronaut consumes oxygen. A separate supply replenishes it. Scrubbing exhaled carbon dioxide alone cannot replace the oxygen the crew uses.
the compressor moves gas from the return: The compressor moves gas from the return side toward the absorber. A separate fan circulates air within the cabin.
two rectangular filter packs fit in the: Two rectangular filter packs fit in the absorber assembly. Lithium hydroxide captured carbon dioxide, and activated charcoal removed odors.
separate gas and water glycol passages e: Separate gas and water-glycol passages exchange heat through their walls. Cooling the breathing gas also causes some moisture to condense.
collected water leaves the breathing gas: Collected water leaves the breathing-gas circuit. The gas returns toward the crew after cooling and moisture removal.
the broad blue path traces the breathing: The broad blue path traces the breathing-gas loop. Moving gold marks indicate the direction of circulation. Their spacing and speed are illustrative.
the narrow copper colored path represent: The narrow copper-colored path represents coolant circulating through the exchanger. Coolant and breathing gas remain in separate passages.
gold marks follow the breathing gas circ: Gold marks follow the breathing-gas circuit. Copper marks follow the separate coolant path through the heat exchanger. The impeller turns as gas circulates.
gas passes through the exposed face of t: Gas passes through the exposed face of the cartridge. The mesh keeps the particles inside. The layered section distinguishes the chemical bed and the odor-removal material. Packing and layer thicknesses are illustrative.
the command module cartridge fits into a: The command-module cartridge fits into a rectangular compartment.
lithium hydroxide chemically removes car: Lithium hydroxide chemically removes carbon dioxide from the circulating gas. The granules shown at the cut face are enlarged.
charcoal adsorbs odors from the circulat: Charcoal adsorbs odors from the circulating gas.
the retaining screen covers the bed face: The retaining screen covers the bed face. Its grid spacing has been enlarged so it is visible.
the cutaway opens the exchanger into its: The cutaway opens the exchanger into its core and two fluid connections. The pressure boundaries keep liquid coolant out of the breathing gas.
a large contact area lets heat move acro: A large contact area lets heat move across the metal between the two streams.
the blue ducts carry the circulating gas: The blue ducts carry the circulating gas to and from the core.

a separate front pipe drops from the out: A separate front pipe drops from the outlet of each manifold-mounted catalyst. Both reach the front silencer.
two sensors upstream and two downstream: Two sensors upstream and two downstream allow the engine controller to compare the exhaust before and after each catalyst. The lead paths are schematic.
bmw lists the front silencer separately: B M W lists the front silencer separately from the two manifold-mounted converters. Open the housing to inspect a schematic silencer section.
twin pipes leave the front silencer and: Twin pipes leave the front silencer and run beside the transmission tunnel.
the center silencer fits between the fro: The center silencer fits between the front and rear sections. Service clamps join replacement sections.
both pipes bend toward the left rear muf: Both pipes bend toward the left rear muffler, inboard of the left wheel. The axle clearance bend is reconstructed.
the stock rear silencer sits on the driv: The stock rear silencer sits on the driver’s side. Its two tailpipes are visible below the bumper. The internal chamber model illustrates silencing principles.
the two closely spaced outlets emerge to: The two closely spaced outlets emerge together at the left side of the rear bumper.
rubber mounts support the exhaust while: Rubber mounts support the exhaust while allowing movement. The sleeved clamps join the service sections.
at a cold start an electric pump supplie: At a cold start an electric pump supplies fresh air to the exhaust ports through a check valve. This helps bring the catalysts up to operating temperature.
start at the water pump and thermostat t: Start at the water pump and thermostat, then follow the radiator loop and the smaller pipes beneath the intake manifold. The heater branch crosses the firewall to the dashboard matrix.
the molded pipe runs beneath the manifol: The molded pipe runs beneath the manifold. The parts plate identifies it as 11 53 1 705 210 and shows the sealing rings separately.
the second molded water pipe follows the: The second molded water pipe follows the block under the inlet manifold. Its body, O-ring ends and a retaining tab are shown.
the solenoid regulates hot coolant to th: The solenoid regulates hot coolant to the heater matrix. Open the valve to follow the plunger and seat.
follow the solenoid plunger as it opens: Follow the solenoid plunger as it opens and closes the water passage.
coolant leaves the engine side inlet pip: Coolant leaves the engine-side inlet pipe, passes through the heater valve and reaches the heater core through the firewall.
the second firewall connection carries c: The second firewall connection carries coolant back to the engine-side water pipe.
the refrigerant loop runs from the belt: The refrigerant loop runs from the belt-driven compressor to the condenser, receiver-drier, expansion valve and evaporator. Cabin air enters through the cowl filter and blower. A separate heater core carries engine coolant.
the condenser sits ahead of the engine r: The condenser sits ahead of the engine radiator. Air passes through its fins as hot refrigerant rejects heat.
liquid refrigerant from the condenser pa: Liquid refrigerant from the condenser passes through a desiccant pack and screen before the expansion valve.
the metering block at the evaporator thr: The metering block at the evaporator throttles the incoming liquid. Both refrigerant lines meet it at the bulkhead.
the low pressure core cools and dehumidi: The low-pressure core cools and dehumidifies the air crossing the HVAC housing.
engine coolant circulates through a sepa: Engine coolant circulates through a separate matrix downstream of the evaporator. The supply and return connections lead back through the firewall.
the narrow lines connect compressor disc: The narrow lines connect compressor discharge, condenser, receiver and metering block in sequence.
the larger low pressure return line carr: The larger low-pressure return line carries refrigerant vapor from the evaporator back to the belt-driven compressor.
an electric motor below the cowl filter: An electric motor below the cowl filter drives two blower wheels on one shaft. Open the motor to see both wheels turn.
the central motor drives both wheels at: The central motor drives both wheels at the same speed.
the control panel requests a fan speed a: The control panel requests a fan speed. A finned power stage varies the blower drive and sheds heat into the airstream.
the long filter sits across the base of: The long filter sits across the base of the windshield, upstream of the blower.
upper branches direct air to the windshi: Upper branches direct air to the windshield and face outlets. The lower outlets supply the footwells.
temperature and fan settings are entered: Temperature and fan settings are entered on the center stack. The controller commands blower output and the flap actuators.
the optional front seat heaters have sep: The optional front seat heaters have separate driver and passenger controls. Each switch cycles through three levels. The switch center uses temperature feedback from each cushion.
the flexible element lies just under the: The flexible element lies just under the center pad of the front seat. Open it to separate the textile, wire and lead.
a second flexible heater follows the sea: A second flexible heater follows the seatback angle. It connects to the seat wiring below.
a temperature sensitive resistor in the: A temperature-sensitive resistor in the cushion feeds the switching center so it can regulate heat.
the under seat connector branches to the: The under-seat connector branches to the cushion and backrest. A flexible loop permits seat movement.
one switch per front seat selects three: One switch per front seat selects three heat settings. Three indicators beside each switch show the selected level.
the battery and front fuse carrier suppl: The battery and front fuse carrier supply the body electronics. GM V operates body conveniences, the light switch center manages exterior lighting and the cluster exchanges information between the K-bus and drivetrain CAN.
the general module sits on the electroni: The general module sits on the electronics carrier behind the glove compartment. Its board and plug layout illustrate the controller and its harness connections.
a high current fuse near the trunk batte: A high-current fuse near the trunk battery supplies the front distribution box. The starter feed and fused body feed serve different loads.
the safety terminal at the positive batt: The safety terminal at the positive battery post separates the starter/alternator feed when triggered. The fused distribution branch is shown separately.
the carrier behind the glovebox locates: The carrier behind the glovebox locates plug-in relays above the body controller. The relay arrangement is schematic.
the lsz combines the driver's lighting c: The LSZ combines the driver’s lighting controls with the electronics that switch and monitor exterior lighting.
the cluster receives drivetrain informat: The cluster receives drivetrain information on CAN and exchanges body information over K-bus. These plugs sit behind the E46 instrument binnacle.
the single wire k bus connects body modu: The single-wire K-bus connects body modules. The junction under the dashboard branches to the general module, light switch center and instrument cluster.
the twisted can pair carries drivetrain: The twisted CAN pair carries drivetrain messages to the instrument cluster. Its path follows the bulkhead schematically.
the belt drives a hydraulic pump that su: The belt drives a hydraulic pump that supplies the front rack. Inside the cabin, a hand lever releases the steering column so the driver can set its height and reach.
the transverse rack is mounted ahead of: The transverse rack is mounted ahead of the front axle. Its tie rods run out to the steering arms on the front wheel carriers.
the pump draws oil from the reservoir an: The pump draws oil from the reservoir and delivers it to the rack. Its section illustrates the changing spaces between the vanes and cam ring.
turn the pulley to follow the vanes arou: Turn the pulley to follow the vanes around the eccentric ring.
the reservoir above the pump provides a: The reservoir above the pump provides a low-pressure supply and receives returning fluid.
the larger low pressure hose connects th: The larger low-pressure hose connects the reservoir outlet to the pump inlet.
a crimped pressure hose carries hydrauli: A crimped pressure hose carries hydraulic fluid to a banjo connection at the steering gear.
rack return pipe and reservoir hose: Rack return pipe and reservoir hose
the low pressure return bends across the: The low-pressure return bends across the front support and returns to the reservoir. The route illustrates the cataloged pipe and hose connections.
the lower shaft carries steering input f: The lower shaft carries steering input from the driver’s column through the bulkhead to the pinion on the rack.
pulling down the lever releases the colu: Pulling down the lever releases the column. Moving the wheel sets reach and height, and raising the lever clamps it in position.

follow cylinder pressure through the pis: Follow cylinder pressure through the piston, connecting rod and crankshaft to the transmission. The block and bearings support that rotating load.
the head closes each cylinder and carrie: The head closes each cylinder and carries the valves. The timing drive keeps valve events synchronized with the crankshaft.
trace filtered air through the meter thr: Trace filtered air through the meter, throttle and manifold to the intake ports. The fuel rail supplies the injectors beside those ports.
electrical energy reaches each combustio: Electrical energy reaches each combustion chamber through its coil and spark plug. The engine controller commands when that discharge occurs.
oil moves from the sump through the pick: Oil moves from the sump through the pickup, pump and filter to loaded surfaces, then drains back. The visible graph shows broad functional links, not every oil gallery.
the pump circulates coolant through the: The pump circulates coolant through the engine and the heat exchanger. The thermostat changes the available flow path as temperature changes.
the crankshaft drives external accessori: The crankshaft drives external accessories through a belt. Separate brackets and engine mounts carry their loads into the engine and body.
the battery supplies electrical power th: The battery supplies electrical power; the engine controller coordinates injection and ignition. The brake-fluid reservoir belongs to the braking circuit, not the engine cooling system.
exhaust ports discharge into the manifol: Exhaust ports discharge into the manifold and onward to the emissions and exhaust system. Catalysts and the full underbody pipework are outside this bay study.
engine core below the cylinder head: Engine core, below the cylinder head
the block holds the cylinder bores and c: The block holds the cylinder bores and crankshaft supports. The head closes its upper deck; the sump closes the lower crankcase. Coolant and oil use separate internal passages.
the crankshaft turns on the main bearing: The crankshaft turns on the main bearings. Connecting rods push on offset crankpins, converting piston travel into rotation; its output end drives the transmission.
between crankshaft journals and the bloc: Between crankshaft journals and the block supports
bearing shells support the crankshaft on: Bearing shells support the crankshaft on a pressure-fed oil film. They are fixed into the block/cap supports while the crankshaft turns inside them.
each rod joins a piston pin to a cranksh: Each rod joins a piston pin to a crankshaft journal. The big end follows the crank circle while the small end follows the piston; their relative angle changes through a revolution.
the piston crowns face the combustion ch: The piston crowns face the combustion chambers. Rings run around their outer grooves, and the rods attach underneath through piston pins. Repeated instances represent the engine’s cylinder count.
the rings form a sliding seal against th: The rings form a sliding seal against the bore and help manage oil on the cylinder wall. They move with the piston; they are not fixed rings inside the block.
between the block deck and head: Between the block deck and head
the gasket seals the combustion openings: The gasket seals the combustion openings while keeping oil and coolant interfaces separated. Its large holes align with the cylinders; smaller passages and bolt holes are simplified here.
the head forms the top of the combustion: The head forms the top of the combustion chamber and contains intake/exhaust ports. Valve seats and guides locate the valves; the camshaft supports sit above them.
the cover encloses the top of the head a: The cover encloses the top of the head and keeps lubricating oil inside. Removing it in this schematic exposes the cam/valve relationship; the view is not a repair sequence.
cam lobes command valve opening through: Cam lobes command valve opening through the engine’s follower arrangement. The timing drive links them to the crankshaft; oil reaches their bearings and moving contact surfaces.
between head ports and combustion chambe: Between head ports and combustion chambers
the valve head seals against its seat wh: The valve head seals against its seat when closed. The stem runs through a guide, and its spring closes it after the cam/follower releases it. Intake and exhaust passages remain separate.
at the timing end of the engine: At the timing end of the engine
the chain transfers crankshaft motion to: The chain transfers crankshaft motion to the cam drive. Guides control its path and a tensioning mechanism manages slack. The chain path is a layout explanation, not a timing-alignment reference.
beside or above the cylinder head intake: Beside or above the cylinder-head intake ports
the plenum distributes air into runners: The plenum distributes air into runners leading to the head ports. Its connection to the throttle is upstream of those runners; injected fuel enters beside the ports in these port-injected engines.
at the outside air entry to the intake p: At the outside-air entry to the intake path
the housing holds the filter element and: The housing holds the filter element and separates the dirty-air inlet from the clean-air outlet. Air then passes into the metering/duct path; joints downstream must seal.
the meter reports incoming air flow to t: The meter reports incoming air flow to the controller. It measures air; it does not pump or throttle it. Its electrical signal and the physical air path are different connections.
the duct carries filtered air toward the: The duct carries filtered air toward the throttle. Bends and resonators address packaging and intake behavior; the displayed route is an approximate connection rather than the molded production hose.
a motor positions the throttle plate to: A motor positions the throttle plate to change the available air passage. The controller commands the actuator; air flows through the body into the manifold.
along the intake port side of the head: Along the intake-port side of the head
the rail supplies pressurized fuel to th: The rail supplies pressurized fuel to the injectors. It is mechanically carried near them but forms a sealed fuel circuit separate from the air manifold and coolant hoses.
at the inlet ports between rail and head: At the inlet ports, between rail and head
each injector meters fuel into an intake: Each injector meters fuel into an intake port under electrical command. Its upper connection receives fuel from the rail; its outlet faces the incoming air near the intake valve.
at or near the spark plug locations: At or near the spark-plug locations
the coils transform low voltage electric: The coils transform low-voltage electrical energy into the high voltage needed at the spark plugs. Their control wiring returns to the engine-management system.
the plug's electrodes project into the c: The plug’s electrodes project into the combustion chamber while its insulated connection remains outside. It bridges the electrical ignition system and the sealed combustion space.
the sump closes the bottom of the engine: The sump closes the bottom of the engine and collects returning oil. The pickup draws from that reservoir; this model does not simulate oil slosh, baffling or fluid level.
at the lower engine lubrication drive: At the lower engine / lubrication drive
the pump draws oil through the pickup an: The pump draws oil through the pickup and supplies the lubrication circuit. Its drive and exact housing position vary by engine; the schematic exposes the pump as a separate part.
the pickup pipe joins the oil reservoir: The pickup pipe joins the oil reservoir to the pump inlet. Its screened entry helps stop larger debris entering the pump; the pickup is not an external oil-filler tube.
external service point on the engine: External service point on the engine
the filter traps contaminants carried by: The filter traps contaminants carried by the oil circuit. The housing’s sealing interfaces and internal valves matter on the real engine but are simplified in the separated geometry.
coolant passes through the heat exchange: Coolant passes through the heat exchanger while air passes across its fins. The upper/lower connections link it to the engine cooling circuit; the fan controls air movement, not coolant pressure.
the fan moves air through the cooling pa: The fan moves air through the cooling pack, especially at low vehicle speed. The shroud guides that air through the intended area. Fan drive and the production blade shape are simplified.
the pump circulates coolant around the e: The pump circulates coolant around the engine and cooling loop. Its inlet/outlet relationship is shown functionally; the model does not calculate pressure or reproduce every bypass.
at the engine's coolant flow junction: At the engine’s coolant flow junction
the thermostat changes the route availab: The thermostat changes the route available to coolant with temperature. It belongs to a housing in the coolant circuit; it does not open the radiator cap or directly switch the fan.
between engine outlet and radiator conne: Between engine outlet and radiator connection
this hose represents the hot side connec: This hose represents the hot-side connection to the radiator. The exact path, quick connectors and branch fittings differ by model; follow the linked diagrams for production routing.
between radiator return and engine inlet: Between radiator return and engine inlet
this hose represents the coolant return: This hose represents the coolant return connection toward the pump. Its relationship to the upper hose completes the main heat-rejection loop; branch and bypass circuits are abbreviated.
beside the cooling pack engine bay: Beside the cooling pack / engine bay
the reservoir provides expansion space a: The reservoir provides expansion space and a service-level reference for the cooling system. Small vent/return lines are only broadly represented and are not interchangeable with radiator hoses.
the alternator converts mechanical rotat: The alternator converts mechanical rotation into electrical output. The belt supplies that rotation; electrical connections link it to the vehicle’s charging system.
around the crank pulley and driven acces: Around the crank pulley and driven accessories
the belt transmits crankshaft power to a: The belt transmits crankshaft power to accessory pulleys. It follows a tensioned loop outside the timing case; it is separate from the timing chain inside the engine.
the tensioner loads an idler pulley agai: The tensioner loads an idler pulley against the belt to maintain useful tension. Its arm/pivot is carried by the engine; the belt runs on the pulley.
the starter engages the ring gear area t: The starter engages the ring-gear area to turn the crankshaft for starting. It uses electrical power for this brief task; it is not continuously driven by the accessory belt.
on the accessory drive side of the engin: On the accessory-drive side of the engine
the compressor belongs to the refrigeran: The compressor belongs to the refrigerant circuit and is mechanically driven by the engine on these layouts. Refrigerant pipework is distinct from coolant, oil and fuel circuits.
between the engine brackets and supporti: Between the engine brackets and supporting structure
the mounts carry the powertrain into the: The mounts carry the powertrain into the vehicle’s structure while controlling transmitted movement. Their rubber/hydraulic internals and load behavior are not modeled.
vehicle specific battery or under hood p: Vehicle-specific battery or under-hood power connection
this marks the electrical supply interfa: This marks the electrical supply interface for the bay. Some cars locate the physical battery elsewhere; the component description identifies that distinction instead of implying every battery sits next to the engine.

round instruments and guarded switches o: Round instruments and guarded switches occupied the front and side panels within reach of the commander.

the eyepiece projected into the cabin be: The eyepiece projected into the cabin between the two crew positions. Astronauts could sight stars through the optical system.
closeout photographs show cloth compartm: Closeout photographs show cloth compartments, helmet bags and tethers around the crew area. Stowage changed between launch, checkout and surface work.
a downward canted triangular opening at: A downward-canted triangular opening at each standing station gave the crew a view of terrain close to the lander.

the square hatch beneath the central ins: The square hatch beneath the central instrument panels swung into the cabin. Beyond the opening lay the porch and ladder.

a straight nine cylinder generator engin: A straight nine-cylinder generator engine supplements eight V20 machines.
the inline nine also drives an alternato: The inline nine also drives an alternator, bringing the total to nine generator sets.
the generators feed a common electrical: The generators feed a common electrical system rather than a separate engine-to-propeller shaft for each thruster.
eight man v20s and one inline nine gener: Eight MAN V20s and one inline nine generate power. Twelve steerable electric thrusters turn that power into thrust.
one of two oil fired boilers supplies st: One of two oil-fired boilers supplies steam to the turbine plant.
steam expands across the turbine stages: Steam expands across the turbine stages. Its shaft connects to the reduction gear ahead of the propeller line.
exhaust steam condenses across a bank of: Exhaust steam condenses across a bank of seawater-cooled tubes. A pump sends condensate back toward the boilers.
the turbine turns much faster than the s: The turbine turns much faster than the single propeller. The reduction gear couples their different speeds.
shafting runs aft from the gear to the s: Shafting runs aft from the gear to the single screw beneath the counter stern.

twelve cylinders fire along a single cra: Twelve cylinders fire along a single crankshaft. The low-speed diesel is coupled directly to the propeller shaft.
the turbochargers compress incoming air: The turbochargers compress incoming air. After cooling, air enters the receiver alongside the cylinder jackets.
exhaust from the engine passes through t: Exhaust from the engine passes through the turbocharger turbines and rises into the red funnel casing above.
the crankshaft flange drives one shaft t: The crankshaft flange drives one shaft. There is no speed-reducing gearbox between this low-speed engine and its propeller.

an independent gas turbine supplies the: An independent gas turbine supplies the center booster jet through reduction gearing.
one of three mtu 16v396 tb94 diesels the: One of three MTU 16V396 TB94 diesels. The three engines deliver power through separate stern waterjets.
a short coupling joins the engine to the: A short coupling joins the engine to the gear. Output shaft speed matches the impeller’s required range.
the impeller draws water up through the: The impeller draws water up through the bottom intake and accelerates it toward the transom discharge.
three v16 diesels each with its own wate: Three V16 diesels, each with its own waterjet, occupy the broad afterbody of the original Heesen yacht.
the 16 cylinder two stroke diesel suppli: The 16-cylinder two-stroke diesel supplies the single controllable-pitch propeller through a reduction gear.
at the documented 900 engine rpm the 7.2: At the documented 900 engine rpm the 7.20:1 gear turns the propeller shaft at 125 rpm.
the gearbox power takeoff drives a 1700: The gearbox power takeoff drives a 1,700 kW generator. It supplies electrical loads from the operating main engine.
the output drives the single screw in it: The output drives the single screw in its nozzle. Pitch change alters the amount of water driven astern at a given shaft speed.
the emd diesel drives a vertically offse: The EMD diesel drives a vertically offset Lufkin gear. One output goes to the propeller, while a power takeoff turns the ABB shaft generator.
the selected series 2000 v16 m96l option: The selected Series 2000 V16 M96L option places a sixteen-cylinder diesel beside the centerline service aisle.
the gearbox connects this engine to its: The gearbox connects this engine to its own inclined propeller shaft.
a shaft carries the engine's torque aft: A shaft carries the engine’s torque aft beneath the fishing cockpit to the propeller.
the available twin mtu v16 installation: The available twin MTU V16 installation sits beneath the saloon. A center aisle separates the engines, which drive independent port and starboard shafts.
lead acid cells supply electrical energy: Lead-acid cells supply electrical energy to the submersible’s propulsion and other onboard loads.
a reversible electric motor turns the sh: A reversible electric motor turns the shrouded propeller. Its installed axis determines which way the thrust acts.
two 120 volt lead acid banks supply seve: Two 120-volt lead-acid banks supply seven thrusters. Three act fore and aft, two act vertically and two act sideways. The side-force units are separated fore and aft.
crossmembers carry the two banks low in: Crossmembers carry the two banks low in the vehicle. The open frame supports the thruster drives around the fairing.
water enters through a bottom opening an: Water enters through a bottom opening and turns toward the closely fitted impeller. The section removes a wall facing the observer.
the input shaft enters from forward its: The input shaft enters from forward. Its rotating hub carries the impeller.
the rotating blades add energy to the wa: The rotating blades add energy to the water. Their outer tips pass close to the stationary wear surface.
a close fitting circular wall surrounds: A close-fitting circular wall surrounds the tips. The opening here exposes the impeller and the stationary row behind it.
these vanes remain stationary they turn: These vanes remain stationary. They turn the swirling discharge from the impeller back toward the jet axis.
a converging passage accelerates the str: A converging passage accelerates the stream as it leaves the stern.
the discharge nozzle can turn on its piv: The discharge nozzle can turn on its pivots to direct the jet sideways.
follow the water from the low hull intak: Follow the water from the low hull intake, through the turning impeller and fixed stator, to the stern nozzle. Blade counts illustrate the pump section.
watch the impeller turn inside the fixed: Watch the impeller turn inside the fixed casing. The stator and discharge nozzle stay still.
the casing surrounds the blade rows the: The casing surrounds the blade rows. The side facing the observer has been removed to reveal the rotor and stationary vanes.
the blades and discs transfer torque to: The blades and discs transfer torque to the shaft. The enlarged end journals locate the rotor in its bearings.
fixed vanes redirect flow between rows o: Fixed vanes redirect flow between rows of rotating compressor and turbine blades.
the rotating front stages raise the pres: The rotating front stages raise the pressure of the intake air before it enters the combustor.
air enters the combustion section after: Air enters the combustion section after the compressor. Hot gas leaves toward the turbine. The liner is shown in section.
energy in the hot gas turns the turbine: Energy in the hot gas turns the turbine wheels. The power turbine drives the central waterjet through reduction gearing.
the two center propulsion lines draw pow: The two center propulsion lines draw power from gas turbines. This section follows air through compression, combustion and expansion. Stage counts and shaft architecture are illustrative.
the gold wheels turn with the rotor watc: The gold wheels turn with the rotor. Watch the stationary guide rows between them.
an energized stator drives a central rot: An energized stator drives a central rotor. This section illustrates the working principle of Alvin’s electric thrusters. Magnet, winding and pole geometry are representative.
the housing locates the stator and suppo: The housing locates the stator and supports the end bearings.
coils sit around the stationary iron cor: Coils sit around the stationary iron core. Their changing magnetic field exerts torque on the rotor.
the central rotor transfers torque direc: The central rotor transfers torque directly into the shaft.
the bearing races locate the rotating sh: The bearing races locate the rotating shaft at each end of the motor.
the propeller pushes water along the thr: The propeller pushes water along the thruster axis. Reversing thrust gives a force in the opposite direction.
the shaft rotor and propeller turn toget: The shaft, rotor and propeller turn together while the copper windings stay fixed.
a smaller input gear drives a larger whe: A smaller input gear drives a larger wheel on a parallel shaft. This cutaway uses one illustrative 2:1 pair to show the speed change.
machined bearing supports align the two: Machined bearing supports align the two shafts and take the gear reaction into the foundation.
the smaller gear turns with the engine i: The smaller gear turns with the engine input. One input revolution advances the larger wheel by half a turn in this example.
the output wheel has twice as many teeth: The output wheel has twice as many teeth. It turns in the opposite direction at half the input speed.
follow a tooth on the gold pinion the la: Follow a tooth on the gold pinion. The larger gear turns more slowly on the output shaft.
seawise giant's two boilers raised steam: Seawise Giant’s two boilers raised steam for the main turbine. This cutaway follows the water and flue-gas sides of a representative marine water-tube boiler.
an open front and side reveal the tube b: An open front and side reveal the tube banks running beside the combustion space.
water and steam separate in the upper dr: Water and steam separate in the upper drum. Steam leaves through an upper connection to the next section.
the tubes meet the lower headers near th: The tubes meet the lower headers near the bottom of the furnace.
water and steam flow inside parallel tub: Water and steam flow inside parallel tubes while hot combustion gas passes outside them.
the burner admits fuel and combustion ai: The burner admits fuel and combustion air to the furnace, on the gas side of the tube walls.
the inboard coupling turns the shaft a s: The inboard coupling turns the shaft. A stern-tube bearing supports it where it passes through the hull, and the propeller pushes water astern.
the shaft transmits torque along its len: The shaft transmits torque along its length from the coupling to the hub.
the flange forms the inboard connection: The flange forms the inboard connection to the engine or reduction gear.
a liner carries the shaft inside a rigid: A liner carries the shaft inside a rigid tube. The facing half is cut away to show the running surface.
the blades rotate together with the hub: The blades rotate together with the hub. This blade pattern is illustrative.
a marked propeller blade turns around th: A marked propeller blade turns around the same centerline as the shaft.
two lead acid banks supply alvin's elect: Two lead-acid banks supply Alvin’s electrical system. Each bank is rated at 120 volts. A single enlarged cell shows the alternating plates.
the battery pack groups cells into a sin: The battery pack groups cells into a single electrical source. The case is sectioned to leave the plate stack visible.
the plates of one polarity share a termi: The plates of one polarity share a terminal strap. Plates of the opposite polarity alternate across the cell.
porous separators keep opposite plates a: Porous separators keep opposite plates apart while allowing ionic conduction through the electrolyte.
the two terminal posts connect the cell: The two terminal posts connect the cell to its neighbors in the bank.
the engine drives the alternator rotor a: The engine drives the alternator rotor. A moving magnetic field induces an alternating voltage in the stationary windings. The cutaway illustrates a generator section, with representative winding and pole counts.
the diesel crankshaft delivers torque to: The diesel crankshaft delivers torque to the generator rotor through a flexible coupling.
the field structure revolves with the in: The field structure revolves with the input shaft inside the fixed windings.
the fixed copper windings collect electr: The fixed copper windings collect electrical energy from the rotating field.
the casing carries the stationary core a: The casing carries the stationary core and the output terminal box. The base feet hold it in line with the drive.
the gold poles rotate with the engine wh: The gold poles rotate with the engine while the outer copper windings remain still.

the hull carries the vertical and horizo: The hull carries the vertical and horizontal loads from the thruster.
the column turns in the mounting ring th: The column turns in the mounting ring. The submerged housing supports the propeller shaft.
the output shaft revolves about its own: The output shaft revolves about its own axis as the steering system aims the entire thrust unit.

the facing halves of each pulley form a: The facing halves of each pulley form a V-shaped groove. The front faces are sectioned to expose the belt where it touches the cones. Narrowing the primary groove sends the belt outward. The belt moves inward on the secondary pulley, changing the two shafts’ relative speed. The cutaway shows the variator section of the H R V transaxle.
one face of the input pulley the engine: One face of the input pulley. The engine turns this shaft through the upstream coupling.
hydraulic pressure changes the spacing o: Hydraulic pressure changes the spacing of the input faces. The belt rides farther from the axis as the groove narrows.
the output pulley passes torque toward t: The output pulley passes torque toward the final reduction. A smaller running radius makes the shaft turn faster for a given belt speed.
the output faces accommodate the complem: The output faces accommodate the complementary running radius and maintain clamping force on the belt.
many small steel elements contact the co: Many small steel elements contact the conical faces. The elements push against their neighbors. Two flexible stacks of steel rings guide them around the loop.
the primary pulley is driven about this: The primary pulley is driven about this axis. The two highlighted pulley faces and the belt expose the changing contact radius.
the driven pulley feeds reduction gears: The driven pulley feeds reduction gears and the front differential.
watch the primary groove narrow the belt: Watch the primary groove narrow, the belt climb outward, and the secondary contact radius shrink. The bronze face on each shaft slides axially. The markers on both pulleys follow the passing belt.
a short enlarged section shows the const: A short, enlarged section shows the construction that repeats around the variator. The sides of each element bear on the conical sheaves.
neighboring steel elements bear against: Neighboring steel elements bear against one another on the transmitting span. The cutouts on both shoulders receive the ring packs.
multiple thin steel loops nest together: Multiple thin steel loops nest together. This short segment enlarges the layers at one shoulder of the elements.
the toothed wheel turns the carrier this: The toothed wheel turns the carrier. This section shows a longitudinal axle-style ring gear. A transverse transaxle generally drives its carrier with parallel-axis reduction gears.
the cross pin is carried around the axle: The cross pin is carried around the axle axis with the final-drive gear. The open frame exposes the differential gears.
the pin turns with the carrier the spide: The pin turns with the carrier. The spider gears can also turn about the pin’s own axis.
the pinion orbits the axle with the carr: The pinion orbits the axle with the carrier and spins about the cross pin whenever the two outputs differ in speed.
splines couple the side gear to its shaf: Splines couple the side gear to its shaft. Its speed can fall below the carrier speed when that wheel follows the inside path.
the two equal size side gears turn at sp: The two equal-size side gears turn at speeds whose average equals carrier speed. The colored end marks help compare them.
the final drive gear turns the carrier t: The final-drive gear turns the carrier. Two spider gears ride on its cross pin and mesh with the side gears on the axle shafts. When the wheels take different paths, the spiders turn on the pin and let one axle advance by the amount the other falls behind. The cutaway shows the common open gearing.
follow the two colored outputs through a: Follow the two colored outputs through a left then a right bend. Their speeds coincide as the paths straighten. The copper spider gears orbit with the frame and spin about the gold pin as the paths diverge.
a gear on the parallel reduction shaft d: A gear on the parallel reduction shaft drives this wheel, which is connected to the differential carrier.
a final reduction gear turns the carrier: A final reduction gear turns the carrier between the front wheels. The spider and side gears share drive between the half-shafts while allowing the wheels to turn at different speeds.
hold the outer ring still and turn the c: Hold the outer ring still and turn the central sun gear. Three small gears walk around the ring and carry their supporting frame along at a lower speed. This section illustrates one planetary reduction in an automatic transmission. The gear counts are chosen to make the motion visible.
the central 16 tooth gear drives all thr: The central 16-tooth gear drives all three planets.
thirty two inward facing teeth provide t: Thirty-two inward-facing teeth provide the reaction for this reduction.
this eight tooth pinion turns about its: This eight-tooth pinion turns about its own pin and orbits the sun as the carrier moves.
the three planet pins share a frame the: The three planet pins share a frame. The output shaft turns with this frame once for every three turns of the sun.
the gold sun makes three turns for each: The gold sun makes three turns for each turn of the carrier. Follow a copper planet as it spins about its pin while its center travels around the stationary ring.
the ignition coil applies voltage to the: The ignition coil applies voltage to the terminal. The center conductor carries it down the ceramic insulator. At the firing end the spark crosses the small gap to the ground electrode and returns through the threaded shell.
the coil or plug lead connects here the: The coil or plug lead connects here. The metal post carries the pulse into the resistor and the center electrode.
the ceramic electrically separates the c: The ceramic electrically separates the center conductor from the shell. The ribs lengthen the possible surface path from the terminal to the shell.
a resistive element in the center path s: A resistive element in the center path suppresses electrical interference generated by the ignition pulse.
conductive glass seals retain the center: Conductive glass seals retain the center stack, provide electrical contact and close off the internal passage.
the conductive core carries heat toward: The conductive core carries heat toward the shell. The exposed alloy tip concentrates the electric field across the gap.
the hex threaded shank and lower rim are: The hex, threaded shank and lower rim are one metal shell. It holds the ceramic and connects the ground electrode electrically to the cylinder head.
on this gasket seat example the metal wa: On this gasket-seat example the metal washer seals the plug against the cylinder head. Actual plug seats and electrodes vary by application.
the curved strap belongs to the shell it: The curved strap belongs to the shell. Its free end faces the center electrode across a small gap.
heat flows inward from the firing tip to: Heat flows inward from the firing tip to the conductive core. The jacket surrounds the core where the plug is exposed to hot gas.
copper conducts heat away from the worki: Copper conducts heat away from the working tip into the plug body.
the jacket encloses the core and present: The jacket encloses the core and presents the firing surface on this representative conventional electrode.

this twenty four tooth illustrative gear: This twenty-four-tooth illustrative gear turns once while its twelve-tooth mate turns twice. Its side dogs engage the selector sleeve.

the crankshaft drives the flywheel its f: The crankshaft drives the flywheel. Its flat face provides one friction surface for the clutch disc.
friction linings on two faces allow the: Friction linings on two faces allow the disc to carry torque when clamped. Its splined hub engages the gearbox input shaft.
the pressure plate clamps the driven dis: The pressure plate clamps the driven disc to the flywheel while the spring acts through the clutch cover.
radial fingers transmit the release forc: Radial fingers transmit the release force. The diagram separates the load-carrying spring from the pressure plate.
the wheel can move on its suspension whi: The wheel can move on its suspension while the driveshaft continues to turn. In this representative fixed joint the cage guides balls in matching tracks in the inner race and outer housing.
the wheel side housing collects torque f: The wheel-side housing collects torque from the balls. A sector is removed here so the balls and cage remain visible.
the balls transfer load between the two: The balls transfer load between the two sets of tracks. Their centers lie in the plane that bisects the angle between the shafts.
the six openings hold the balls around t: The six openings hold the balls around the inner race and allow each ball to project into the tracks on either side.
grooves on the inner race support the ba: Grooves on the inner race support the balls. The race is splined to the shaft.
the convoluted rubber boot retains greas: The convoluted rubber boot retains grease while allowing the joint to flex.

the rocker pivots where it meets the bod: The rocker pivots where it meets the body and carries the front wheel at its forward end.

both arms pivot about fixed length links: Both arms pivot about fixed-length links as the three wheel centers move relative to one another.
